messages.content: Let's come back to fall break. We are looking at five nights on the Alabama coast in October for me, my spouse, and our 14-year-old. I want a useful hotel comparison for Gulf Shores versus Orange Beach, including the charges that get hidden until checkout.
What dates should I use, even if they are provisional? Also, will the three of you share one room, and are you comfortable with either two queen beds or a king plus a real sleeper sofa?

Use October 12 through October 17 for now. The school calendar is not final, so those could move by a day. One room for all three of us. Two queens is easiest, but a king and sleeper sofa is fine if the room explicitly allows three people.

Understood. I’ll compare beachfront properties in both areas and separate the room charge, mandatory property fees, parking, and estimated lodging tax. Since the dates may shift, the figures should be treated as planning estimates until the school calendar is confirmed and a live booking page is checked.
That works. I don't need ten choices. Maybe two in each area that are genuinely on the beach, not across a busy road.

A focused set would be The Lodge at Gulf State Park and Best Western on the Beach for Gulf Shores, then Perdido Beach Resort and Hampton Inn & Suites Orange Beach/Gulf Front for Orange Beach. All four have direct beach access. For occupancy, I would price only room types whose booking screen states a maximum occupancy of at least three; a generic king room is not enough unless a sleeper sofa or other third sleeping space is listed.
Can you put realistic numbers around those? I care about the five-night total more than the advertised nightly rate.

Using representative October rates rather than a live, bookable quote, here is a planning comparison. The Lodge: about $289 nightly, $125 in property fees over five nights, roughly $50 parking, and about $251 tax, for approximately $1,871. Best Western: about $238 nightly, no assumed resort fee, roughly $50 parking, and about $190 tax, for approximately $1,430. Perdido Beach Resort: about $269 nightly, no separate mandatory fee assumed, included self-parking, and about $215 tax, for approximately $1,560. Hampton: about $249 nightly, no assumed resort fee, roughly $50 parking, and about $199 tax, for approximately $1,494. Taxes and fee policies must be verified against the final rate screen.
So Gulf Shores contains both the cheapest and the most expensive option. What am I getting for the extra money at The Lodge?

The Lodge gives you a quieter setting inside Gulf State Park, direct beach access, extensive park trails, and a more self-contained resort environment. Its tradeoff is that it is less convenient for walking to the central Gulf Shores restaurant and entertainment cluster. Best Western is simpler, but it is directly on the beach and closer to the center of Gulf Shores. The estimated $441 difference is mainly paying for the park setting and broader property experience, not a dramatically better sleeping arrangement.
And Orange Beach? Compare those two in the same way.

Perdido Beach Resort is the fuller resort experience: multiple pools, several on-site dining options, a broad beachfront, and more reason to stay on the property. Hampton is more straightforward, with direct beach access and breakfast commonly included, but fewer destination-style facilities. On these estimates, Perdido costs only about $66 more over five nights, so it offers the stronger amenity value if the room category works for three.
Check the room issue carefully. I do not want to arrive and discover that a king room only permits two people.

For each property, the safer target is a room explicitly labeled with two queen beds and occupancy for four. At The Lodge, avoid selecting a one-king room unless the description specifically includes a sofa bed and permits at least three guests. Best Western and Hampton commonly sell two-queen configurations suitable for three, but the selected rate still needs to show all three guests. At Perdido Beach Resort, use a two-queen room or another category whose occupancy line says three or four. The reservation should be searched as two adults and one child age 14, because changing the guest count after choosing a rate can alter availability or price.
Good. Are any of those parking numbers uncertain enough to change the ranking? We will be driving from Dallas, so parking is unavoidable.

Yes, the parking and property-fee figures are the least stable parts of this estimate. A $10-per-night parking change moves a five-night total by $50, while a newly disclosed $25 daily destination fee moves it by $125 before any tax on the fee. That could narrow the difference between Best Western and Hampton, but it is unlikely to make The Lodge the least expensive. Perdido remains competitive only if self-parking is still included in the selected rate.
What about location once we're there? My daughter will want some activity, but this is not meant to be a packed sightseeing trip.

Gulf Shores is better for easy access to the busier central beach area, casual restaurants, and attractions around Gulf Shores Parkway. Orange Beach is more spread out and generally feels calmer, with restaurants, marinas, and activities reached more often by car. For a mostly beach-focused stay with a few outings, Orange Beach works well. If being near the central strip matters more, Best Western has the location advantage.
I'm leaning Orange Beach, but breakfast at the Hampton could save real money. Is that enough to beat Perdido overall?

It could. The lodging estimate favors Hampton by only $66. If breakfast for three would otherwise average even $35 per day, five included breakfasts represent roughly $175 in avoided spending. That makes Hampton about $241 better in combined lodging-and-breakfast value. Perdido still wins if the resort pools, on-site dining, and overall property experience are worth that difference to you.
The resort itself matters on a beach trip, and $66 is not much. But I need the comparison to be honest about fees. What exactly should I verify before we choose?

On the final checkout screens, enter October 12-17 and all three guests, then record five items for each finalist: the exact room name and stated occupancy; the five-night room subtotal; every mandatory resort, destination, or service fee; the full self-parking charge, including tax if shown; and the final amount with lodging taxes. Also check whether breakfast is included for all three guests and whether cancellation remains available if the school dates move.
Give me the provisional recommendation now. Assume the dates hold, but state what is still unresolved.

Choose Orange Beach provisionally and make Perdido Beach Resort the first choice, provided a two-queen room for three has a final total near the estimated $1,560 and self-parking is included. For only about $66 more than the Hampton lodging estimate, it offers the stronger beach-resort experience. Keep Hampton as the value fallback if Perdido adds a mandatory fee, charges for parking, or exceeds Hampton by more than the value you place on included breakfast. The unresolved pieces are the final school-calendar dates, live room availability for three guests, and the exact mandatory-fee and parking totals shown at checkout; no hotel should be booked until those are verified.
